title: meme scene contract v3 (P2 capability set)
description: Declarative scene for the meme runtime. v3 accepts exactly what P2 can execute: spheres and planes; materials with base_color, metallic, roughness, ior and two-sided emission (GGX microfacet + exact dielectric Fresnel, Schlick for metals, a delta lobe below roughness^2 = 1e-3); point lights; constant/split environment; pinhole camera; rigid sphere bodies under XPBD (Mueller et al. 2020 with substeps, Macklin et al. 2019) with sphere/plane contacts, restitution, static and dynamic friction, and distance / ball / hinge / fixed joints. Every float carries x-unit plus minimum/maximum. Cross-field rules live in x-semantic-checks and are enforced before any GPU work. v1 and v2 scenes are migrated on load (x-migrations).

v.description: Schema version, bound to golden set p2. v1 and v2 scenes are accepted and migrated (x-migrations). Not patchable.

materials.description: Id-keyed map. Key order in the JSON text carries no meaning; the runtime iterates in byte order of the key.

objects.description: Id-keyed map of renderable and/or simulated objects. A sphere with `body` is dynamic; everything else is static.

physics_materials.description: Id-keyed map of contact materials (restitution, friction).

joints.description: Id-keyed map of joints between rigid bodies or a body and the world. Requires physics.

lights.description: Id-keyed map of lights that are not geometry. Emissive spheres are area lights automatically.

Seed.description: Global seed. Every random source is rng(stream, counter) = Philox4x32-10(key=(seed, stream), counter). See x-rng-streams.

Id.description: Entity id. Lowercase ASCII so JSON Pointer paths need no escaping (/objects/ball_1/radius_m).

Meta.description: Free text, excluded from scene_hash. Never read by the runtime.

Vec3_Dir_1.description: Direction; normalized by the runtime in f64. Norm must be >= 1e-3 (E_ZERO_VECTOR).

Color_1.description: Linear Rec.709 RGB, each channel in [0,1].

Environment.description: Infinitely distant emitter seen by rays that hit nothing. Radiance RGB = luminance_cdm2 * color / Y(color), Y = BT.709 luma weights.

oneOf.description: Directions d with dot(d, up) > 0 see upper_cdm2, the rest see lower_cdm2. Gives analytic irradiance (1+cos(theta))/2 on tilted planes.

spp.description: Fixed samples per pixel. Sample s of pixel p always uses counter (px, py, s, dim); pass/tile splitting must not change output bytes.

max_bounces.description: Number of scattering events. Emission is collected at surface interactions 1..max_bounces+1 (by hitting emitters, or for nee/mis by light sampling at interactions 1..max_bounces); the environment is collected by any escaping ray or by light sampling. No Russian roulette.

display_white_cdm2.description: Linear radiance mapped to display 1.0 before clamp + sRGB OETF in the PNG. Does not affect the linear PFM.

strategy.description: Estimator: bsdf = BSDF sampling only; nee = light sampling for every samplable light (BSDF hits on them count 0); mis = both, weighted by the power heuristic. All three are unbiased.

integrator.description: XPBD rigid bodies (Mueller et al. 2020): per step, `substeps` substeps of length h = dt_s / substeps, each one Jacobi iteration with mass splitting (Tonge et al. 2012), then a velocity pass for restitution and dynamic friction. Positions are Q31.32 fixed point and velocities follow the delta form v = (h v + g h^2 + dx_corr) / h; without contacts and joints this is exactly the v2 integrator xpbd_unconstrained_p0.

record_every_steps.description: State snapshot at step 0, every k steps, and at the final step.

substeps.description: Substeps per step, each with one solver iteration (Macklin et al. 2019, Small Steps).

contacts.description: none: bodies pass through everything. all_pairs: every dynamic sphere collides with every other sphere and with every plane (O(n^2) per substep).

Material.description: metallic blends a GGX conductor (F0 = base_color, Schlick) with a dielectric: a GGX coat with exact Fresnel at ior over a Lambert base coupled for energy conservation. alpha = roughness^2 (Burley 2012); alpha < 1e-3 is a delta lobe. Defaults reproduce the v1 Lambert material exactly. Emission is two-sided Lambertian.

Body.description: Makes a sphere a rigid body (solid sphere, inertia 2/5 m r^2). center_m and orientation are the state at step 0.

physics_material.description: Key of physics_materials; omitted means restitution 0 and no friction.

oneOf.description: Infinite static plane through point_m. Rendering: two-sided, rays with |dot(dir, normal)| < 2^-20 are treated as parallel (miss). Physics: a solid half-space below the plane; normal points into free space.

physics_material.description: Key of physics_materials; omitted means restitution 0 and no friction.

PatchEnvelope.description: The only interaction unit. Applied atomically to the scene whose hash is base_scene_hash, then the whole result is re-validated (schema + semantic). Any failure leaves the scene unchanged.

PatchOp.description: RFC 6902 operation. `value` is checked after application by validating the resulting scene.

Ior_1.description: Index of refraction of the dielectric coat; 1 means no specular interface (pure Lambert when metallic = 0).

oneOf.description: Point light radiating intensity_cd in every direction; RGB intensity = intensity_cd * color / Y(color).

Quat_1.description: Unit quaternion [x, y, z, w] rotating body-frame vectors into the world frame; | |q| - 1 | must be <= 1e-6 (E_NORM).

PhysicsMaterial.description: Contact response. Two objects in contact combine as sqrt(friction_a * friction_b) and max(restitution_a, restitution_b) (Box2D b2MixFriction / b2MixRestitution). An object without physics_material uses restitution 0 and no friction.

restitution.description: Newton's coefficient of restitution; applied to the pre-solve normal velocity, and taken as 0 when that is at most 2 |g| h (Mueller et al. 2020).

static_friction.description: Static friction coefficient, enforced as a positional constraint.

dynamic_friction.description: Dynamic (Coulomb) friction coefficient, applied at velocity level; must not exceed static_friction (E_FRICTION_ORDER).

a.description: Object id of a dynamic sphere, or "world".

b.description: Object id of a dynamic sphere, or "world".

anchor_a_m.description: Attachment point on a: in a's body frame, or a world point when a is "world".

anchor_b_m.description: Attachment point on b, as for a.

compliance_m_N.description: 0 is a rigid rod; > 0 is a spring of stiffness 1 / compliance (XPBD alpha, Macklin et al. 2016).

oneOf.description: Keeps the two anchors coincident (spherical joint).

anchor_a_m.description: Attachment point on a: in a's body frame, or a world point when a is "world".

anchor_b_m.description: Attachment point on b, as for a.

oneOf.description: Ball joint plus the two axes kept parallel.

anchor_a_m.description: Attachment point on a: in a's body frame, or a world point when a is "world".

anchor_b_m.description: Attachment point on b, as for a.

axis_a.description: Hinge axis in a's body frame (world frame for "world").

axis_b.description: Hinge axis in b's body frame (world frame for "world").

oneOf.description: Ball joint plus the relative orientation at step 0 kept (weld).

units.m/N: metre per newton (XPBD compliance alpha, the inverse of a stiffness)

x-rng-streams.algorithm: Philox4x32-10, Salmon et al. 2011 'Parallel Random Numbers: As Easy as 1, 2, 3' (SC11); KAT vectors from Random123 kat_vectors
x-rng-streams.id_word: idhash32(id) = FNV-1a 32 of the UTF-8 id; distinct within its map or E_ID_HASH_COLLISION

0.name: sampling
0.dim_block: 0 = pixel jitter (u0,u1); 1+b = bounce b BSDF sample: (u0,u1) direction, u2 lobe choice, u3 reserved; 0x80000000+b = bounce b light sample: u0 light choice, (u1,u2) point or direction on the light, u3 reserved

4.name: harness_fuzz
4.owner: oracle tooling only, never the runtime

5.name: harness_schedule
5.owner: oracle tooling only: tile/dispatch order permutation

6.name: substrate_probe
6.owner: FBH float-behaviour probe inputs; key seed is fixed, independent of any scene

rules: Stream ids are never reused or renumbered.
Scene work may only use streams 0-3; 4-5 belong to the test harness; 6 only feeds the substrate probe.

steps: strict parse: reject duplicate keys (E_DUPLICATE_KEY) and non-finite numbers (E_NONFINITE)
validate against this schema, then x-semantic-checks
serialize with RFC 8785 JSON Canonicalization Scheme

x-semantic-checks.rule: every objects.*.material is a key of materials; every objects.*.physics_material is a key of physics_materials
render present => camera and environment present
|look_at_m - position_m| >= 1e-3 * max(1, |position_m|) and |normalize(up) x normalize(look_at_m - position_m)| >= 1e-3
|v| >= 1e-3 for camera.up, plane normal, environment.up, hinge axes
sphere radius_m >= 2^-12 * (|center_m| + radius_m), leaving >= 12 bits of f32 mantissa for hit-point precision
luminance or intensity > 0 => Y(color) >= 1e-3 with Y = 0.2126 R + 0.7152 G + 0.0722 B (ITU-R BT.709); applies to the environment, emissive materials and lights

physics without contacts and joints, if |g| > 0, for every dynamic body: |g| * h >= 2^-16 * V with h = dt_s / substeps and V = |velocity_m_s| + |g| * dt_s * steps (exact speed bound for free flight). Guarantees each substep's velocity increment is >= 128 ulp(V), so gravity cannot be rounded away in f32. With contacts or joints no a-priori speed bound exists; the run checks the same inequality against the largest speed reached (validator precision.physics).

width_px * height_px * spp * (max_bounces + 1) * max(1, |objects|) * (strategy == bsdf ? 1 : 2) <= 2^36; physics without contacts and joints: |bodies| * steps * substeps <= 2^32; otherwise |bodies| * (|bodies| + |static spheres| + |planes| + |joints|) * steps * substeps <= 2^36
idhash32 distinct among object ids, among material ids, among light ids, among physics material ids and among joint ids
no point light lies inside or on a sphere: |position_m - center_m| > radius_m
contacts all_pairs: at step 0 no dynamic sphere penetrates another sphere or a plane's half-space by more than 2^-20 * radius_m (sum of radii for sphere pairs)

contacts all_pairs or any joint: max(mass_kg) / min(mass_kg) over dynamic bodies <= 100. A 4-high stack with the heavy body on top keeps penetration <= 1e-3 r at mass ratio 100 (dt 1/240 s, 32 substeps) but not at 1000 (design P2D10: the limit is tightened, the penetration bound is not widened; golden G41)
for every dynamic body: |angular_velocity_rad_s| * h <= 0.5 rad, h = dt_s / substeps
every physics material has dynamic_friction <= static_friction
joints require physics; a and b are "world" or ids of dynamic spheres; at least one of them is a sphere
a joint's a and b differ

x-error-codes.report_shape: { code, path (JSON Pointer into the instance), op_index? (patches), detail }

x-patch-rules.result_validation: full schema + semantic checks on the patched scene; atomic on failure
x-patch-rules.conformance: must pass json-patch-tests (github.com/json-patch/json-patch-tests) tests.json and spec_tests.json

chain.migrate: add metallic 0, roughness 1, ior 1 to every material; render.integrator pt_bsdf_p0 -> pt_p1 with strategy bsdf; v = 2. Image, AOV and state bytes are unchanged.
chain.rollback: lossless only if every material has metallic 0 and ior 1, there are no lights and strategy is bsdf; otherwise E_ROLLBACK_LOSSY lists the paths that would be dropped

chain.migrate: physics.integrator xpbd_unconstrained_p0 -> xpbd_p2 with substeps 1 and contacts none; v = 3. Image, AOV and state bytes are unchanged (golden G46).
chain.rollback: lossless only if physics has substeps 1 and contacts none, there are no joints and no physics_materials, no object names a physics_material, and every body has zero angular velocity and the identity orientation; otherwise E_ROLLBACK_LOSSY lists the paths that would be dropped

x-migrations.rule: v(n) -> v(n+1) ships migrate_vN_to_vN+1 and rollback_vN+1_to_vN. Rollback is lossless or fails with E_ROLLBACK_LOSSY. Every golden goes through migrate -> rollback -> migrate with an identical scene_hash. The runtime executes only the latest version; older scenes are migrated on load.
